title: Planning a deep clean alongside routine work
audience: Team leads and cleaners who plan or carry out periodic enhanced cleaning in healthcare, residential care, clinics and commercial buildings, where the site stays in use while the work happens.
learningOutcomes: Describe how a deep clean differs from routine cleaning, and why routine cleaning continues while it is planned and carried out.
List the conditions that justify a deep clean: built-up soil, hard-to-reach areas, and surfaces that the routine cannot restore.
Plan a deep clean with a written method, agreed access and a signed record of the result.

instruction.heading: What a deep clean is
instruction.body: A deep clean is an enhanced programme of work on the same surfaces, not a separate kind of cleaning. It usually brings extra equipment, a stronger approved method or a specialist skill, and it targets soil that has gathered gradually or areas that the routine cannot reach each cycle. It does not replace routine cleaning. The usual schedule continues, and the enhanced work is fitted around it.

instruction.heading: When a deep clean is justified
instruction.body: Look for grime that collects on edges, fixtures and skirting and does not lift with routine wiping; for marks that remain after the approved routine method has been used correctly; for areas with restricted access behind or beneath fixed items; and for high-use zones where daily work has fallen behind. Also check whether the finish itself is the cause. A worn or damaged surface can keep collecting soil, and the remedy may be repair or replacement, not more scrubbing. A space that is easier to reach and clean needs less deep work over time.

instruction.heading: Planning around people who are using the space
instruction.body: Enhanced work is often noisy, wet or uses stronger products, so it can disrupt the people using the site. Sequence the work so occupants are affected as little as possible. Agree access times with the site lead, use barriers and signs, and keep the routine service running in the areas not being worked. Where the site has clinical, care or customer roles, consult those people before the start, not after.

instruction.heading: Recording the result
instruction.body: Keep a record that shows the scope, the reason, the method, the products used, the equipment, the areas completed, any item that was replaced or sent for repair, and a sign-off by both the cleaning lead and the site lead. The record is the audit trail. It lets a later inspection show what was done, when, and by whom, and it shows what was not done and why.

procedure: Identify the area and the reason for the deep clean: soil build-up, restricted access, or a finish that no longer cleans.
Confirm with the site lead that the routine schedule will continue, and agree access times, noise limits and any closure.
Write a short method for each surface: equipment, approved product, order of work and the stopping point for each stage.
Confirm that the specialist equipment, training or supplier the method needs is in place. Do not start a task you are not trained or authorised to do.
Carry out the enhanced work from the cleanest area toward the most soiled, keeping routine service running in the other areas.
Record any surface that does not reach the agreed standard, and raise a repair or replacement request for it.
Inspect the finished area against the criteria agreed in the method and note any defect that remains.
Obtain signatures from the cleaning lead and the site lead on the completed record, and file it with the job record.

workedExamples.situation: A medical clinic's waiting room has grime behind a fixed bench and along the skirting that routine mopping does not lift. The room must stay open for patients during the day.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you schedule the deep clean during opening hours?
workedExamples.reasoning: Not without a plan. Agree a time outside the busiest period with the site lead, or work one section at a time with barriers in place. Write the method first, including the product for the skirting and the order for the bench area. Keep routine service running in the rest of the clinic, and file the signed record afterwards.

workedExamples.situation: A staff room's wall tiles near the sink have a sticky film, and the grout is cracked in two places. Repeated scrubbing has not lifted the film.
workedExamples.reasoning: Not on its own. The cracked grout is a finish problem that will keep trapping soil, so record it and raise a repair request. Use the approved method for the film, note on the record where scrubbing failed, and do not keep working on a damaged finish, which can drive soil into the damage.

equipmentAndPpe: Equipment suited to the enhanced task, used only by people trained for it
Approved products listed on the method, with their safety data sheets available on site
Barriers, signs and wet floor signs for the work zone
Record form for the scope, method, defects and sign-off
Gloves and eye protection, as the product label and task require

commonErrors.error: Treating a deep clean as a reason to stop routine cleaning elsewhere.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the routine schedule running and plan the enhanced work around it.

commonErrors.error: Scrubbing a damaged finish that keeps collecting soil.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the finish defect and request repair or replacement, and say on the record where the method failed.

commonErrors.error: Starting work without an agreed access time or a written method.
commonErrors.prevention: Agree access and sequencing with the site lead, and write the method before the first stroke.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Enhanced work often uses stronger products, plug-in machines or work above floor level. Follow the product label, the safety data sheet and the site rules for each.

Specialist or contractor enhanced work needs a method statement and a risk assessment before it starts (see “Letting a contractor onto a live site: plan, sign-in and sign-off”). Completing this lesson does not qualify anyone to do specialist work.
The UK procedure describes deep cleaning in general terms and gives UK cleaning frequency figures. Those figures are not used here and are not Australian facts.

qualityStandard: Deep clean method written and agreed before the start.
Routine schedule continued in areas not being worked.
Every surface that was replaced, repaired or not brought to standard is recorded with a request raised.
Final inspection signed by the cleaning lead and the site lead.
documentationEvidence: Scope and reason for the deep clean
Method, products used and equipment list
Access times and the site lead's agreement
Defects and any repair or replacement requests
summary: A deep clean is enhanced work on the same surfaces, and routine cleaning continues alongside it.
A damaged finish may need repair, not more scrubbing.
Each deep clean has a written method, agreed access and a signed record.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the relationship between a deep clean and routine cleaning?
options: A deep clean replaces routine cleaning for as long as the enhanced work lasts.
A deep clean is enhanced work that sits alongside routine cleaning, which continues.
Routine cleaning is only needed after the deep clean is finished.

knowledgeChecks.question: A surface keeps collecting soil after careful cleaning, because the finish is worn. What is the best next step?
options: Scrub harder with a stronger product at each visit.
Record the finish defect and request repair or replacement.
Leave it, because wear is normal and is not a cleaning matter.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before an enhanced clean starts in an occupied area, what must be in place?
options: An agreed access plan and a written method with a sign-off step.
The cleaner's own preference for which product to use.
A decision to pause the routine schedule so staff can focus on the deep clean.
